previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A female patient with end-stage renal disease, systemic lupus erythematosus, and antiphospholipid syndrome was admitted for acute dyspnea and profound fatigue. She presented with symptoms concerning for hyperkalemia, including generalized weakness and exertional dyspnea. Labs confirmed hyperkalemia (K 6.3) and metabolic acidosis, and imaging revealed mild pulmonary edema due to fluid overload. She underwent emergent hemodialysis with successful correction of electrolyte abnormalities and symptomatic improvement. Her subtherapeutic INR (1.4) was addressed with a supplemental warfarin dose, and she was advised to continue her home medications, including those for GERD and dry eyes. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to maintain dialysis, monitor symptoms, and follow up for INR monitoring.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  Ataxia.  Assess for stroke or intracranial hemorrhage.

TECHNIQUE:  Contiguous axial MDCT images of the brain were obtained without
administration of IV contrast.  Reformatted coronal, sagittal, and thin
section bone algorithm reconstructed images were acquired.

COMPARISION: CT head without contrast ___. 

DLP:  891.93 mGy-cm.

FINDINGS:  There is no evidence of hemorrhage, edema, mass effect, or mojor
infarction.  Mild prominence of ventricles and sulci is consistent with
age-related cortical volume loss.  The basal cisterns are patent, and there is
preservation of gray-white matter differentiation.

No fracture or soft tissue hematoma.  The globes are unremarkable.  Moderate
mucosal thickening of bilateral sphenoid sinuses is noted.  Additional
visualized paranasal sinuses, mastoid air cells, and middle ear cavities are
clear.

IMPRESSION:  Chronic changes as described above, otherwise negative head CT. 
Specifically, no fracture, acute infarction, or intracranial hemorrhage.

Wet read entered by Dr. ___ on ___ within 5 minutes of
observation of findings stating no acute abnormality.  No cytotoxic edema,
hemorrhage, or acute infarction.

HISTORY:  ___ man with question of stroke.  Renal failure.

TECHNIQUE:  Technique:  Multiplanar, multisequence MRI of the head was
performed without intravenous contrast administration.

COMPARISON:  MRI head without contrast ___, CT head without
contrast ___.

FINDINGS:

There is no evidence of slow diffusion to suggest acute infarct.  There is no
hemorrhage, midline shift, mass effect or extra-axial fluid collections.  The
ventricles, sulci and basilar cisterns are stable with generalized prominence
of the ventricles and sulci consistent with generalized cerebral volume loss. 
Several scattered foci of T2/FLAIR hyperintensity are noted throughout the
deep and periventricular white matter, likely sequela of chronic microvascular
ischemic change. 

Adequate flow voids are seen in the major intracranial vessels.  There is
persistent partial opacification of the bilateral sphenoid sinuses.  There is
a small amount of fluid in the bilateral mastoid air cells, improved from
prior exam.  The orbits and soft tissues are grossly unremarkable.  Visualized
bone marrow signal is unremarkable.  

IMPRESSION:

No evidence of acute intracranial process, including no evidence of infarct,
hemorrhage or mass effect.
